items.text: Factor the denominator and compare degrees.
Use partial fractions, including one term for every repeated-pole power.
Complete squares for conjugate poles and apply time or frequency shifts.
Transform the result forward to check it.
An algebraic expression without a region of convergence does not by itself select a unique sided signal.
The Bromwich parameter must lie to the right of the poles for the usual one-sided causal inversion.
Equality of ordinary inverse transforms is understood up to isolated values; impulses require a distributional interpretation.
A repeated pole needs every lower denominator power in the decomposition.
